findings.title: Workout execution is a long-form set ledger rather than a focused training workspace
findings.evidence: E26/E35/E42/E48/E52/E60 show 12 set rows and four exercise groups in one continuous page; at 390×844 only the first exercise is above the fold.
findings.current_behavior: E26/E35/E42/E48/E52/E60 show 12 set rows and four exercise groups in one continuous page; at 390×844 only the first exercise is above the fold.
findings.root_ux_cause: The data model is rendered directly without a current-exercise/session focus layer.
findings.why_it_matters: The user must act under time, attention and recovery constraints.
findings.user_impact: Repeated scan/scroll and loss of next-action focus during a physical session.
findings.recommended_change: Add current-exercise focus, sticky progress/rest, explicit next/previous and compact set navigation.
findings.why_this_change: It reduces friction while preserving the current capability contract.
findings.expected_benefit: Clearer task completion and higher confidence.
findings.do_not_break: Existing successful route, state persistence and primary actions
findings.implementation_guidance: Add current-exercise focus, sticky progress/rest, explicit next/previous and compact set navigation.

findings.title: Mobile shell hides navigation behind a hamburger during an active fitness workflow
findings.evidence: E29-E48 show top hamburger and no persistent bottom nav; frequent navigation requires opening a drawer.
findings.current_behavior: E29-E48 show top hamburger and no persistent bottom nav; frequent navigation requires opening a drawer.
findings.root_ux_cause: Desktop sidebar compression is used without task-specific mobile navigation.
findings.why_it_matters: The user must act under time, attention and recovery constraints.
findings.user_impact: Extra taps and interruption risk for one-handed users.
findings.recommended_change: Keep drawer for low-frequency destinations but add explicit in-workout reachable navigation and safe exit semantics.
findings.why_this_change: It reduces friction while preserving the current capability contract.
findings.expected_benefit: Clearer task completion and higher confidence.
findings.do_not_break: Existing successful route, state persistence and primary actions
findings.implementation_guidance: Keep drawer for low-frequency destinations but add explicit in-workout reachable navigation and safe exit semantics.

findings.title: Repeated workout inputs lack sufficiently specific accessible names
findings.evidence: E26/E35/E42 AX snapshots expose many unnamed textboxes beside named 0-5/0-10 fields; source relies on visual grouping.
findings.current_behavior: E26/E35/E42 AX snapshots expose many unnamed textboxes beside named 0-5/0-10 fields; source relies on visual grouping.
findings.root_ux_cause: Labels are not consistently bound to exercise, set index and metric.
findings.why_it_matters: The user must act under time, attention and recovery constraints.
findings.user_impact: Keyboard/screen-reader users cannot reliably distinguish repeated fields.
findings.recommended_change: Use unique names, fieldsets and timer/rest live-region semantics for each exercise/set/metric.
findings.why_this_change: It reduces friction while preserving the current capability contract.
findings.expected_benefit: Clearer task completion and higher confidence.
findings.do_not_break: Existing successful route, state persistence and primary actions
findings.implementation_guidance: Use unique names, fieldsets and timer/rest live-region semantics for each exercise/set/metric.

findings.current_behavior: E15/E31/E38/E45/E51/E53/E57 show repeated 'Imagen no disponible todavía' cards and mixed exercise naming.
findings.root_ux_cause: Unavailable media has no compact instructional fallback hierarchy.
findings.why_it_matters: The user must act under time, attention and recovery constraints.
findings.user_impact: More scanning and weaker confidence before opening detail.
findings.recommended_change: Use a compact category/icon placeholder and prioritize name, target muscle and level.
findings.why_this_change: It reduces friction while preserving the current capability contract.
findings.expected_benefit: Clearer task completion and higher confidence.
findings.do_not_break: Existing successful route, state persistence and primary actions
findings.implementation_guidance: Use a compact category/icon placeholder and prioritize name, target muscle and level.

findings.title: AI proposal explains profile rules but not controllable result rationale or reversibility
findings.evidence: E14/E20/E30/E37/E44/E56 show proposal, 40+ rationale, controls and AI CTA; no result/regenerate/undo was safely invoked.
findings.current_behavior: E14/E20/E30/E37/E44/E56 show proposal, 40+ rationale, controls and AI CTA; no result/regenerate/undo was safely invoked.
findings.root_ux_cause: Rationale is attached to profile heuristics, not to a reversible generation state.
findings.why_it_matters: The user must act under time, attention and recovery constraints.
findings.user_impact: Uncertainty about what the plan uses and how to recover from an unwanted result.
findings.recommended_change: Show inputs used, post-generation rationale, edit/regenerate and discard/undo.
findings.why_this_change: It reduces friction while preserving the current capability contract.
findings.expected_benefit: Clearer task completion and higher confidence.
findings.do_not_break: Existing successful route, state persistence and primary actions
findings.implementation_guidance: Show inputs used, post-generation rationale, edit/regenerate and discard/undo.

findings.title: Progress low-data KPIs can read as failure despite a useful recommendation
findings.evidence: E16/E22/E32/E39/E46/E58 show 0 weekly adherence, 0 kg volume, missing trend and a consistency recommendation.
findings.current_behavior: E16/E22/E32/E39/E46/E58 show 0 weekly adherence, 0 kg volume, missing trend and a consistency recommendation.
findings.root_ux_cause: Numeric status is more visually dominant than history coverage/confidence.
findings.why_it_matters: The user must act under time, attention and recovery constraints.
findings.user_impact: Early users may see absence as failure rather than a next step.
findings.recommended_change: Pair low-data values with period, confidence and one above-fold next action.
findings.why_this_change: It reduces friction while preserving the current capability contract.
findings.expected_benefit: Clearer task completion and higher confidence.
findings.do_not_break: Existing successful route, state persistence and primary actions
findings.implementation_guidance: Pair low-data values with period, confidence and one above-fold next action.

findings.title: Nutrition and gamification do not yet expose a shared next-action loop
findings.evidence: E17/E18/E23/E24/E33/E34/E40/E41/E47/E59 plus the selective surface review.
findings.current_behavior: Both are real readable workspaces, but their current UI presents parallel states rather than an explicit bridge from workout behavior to nutrition or XP action.
findings.root_ux_cause: Feature routes are organized as peer dashboards rather than a coordinated weekly narrative.
findings.why_it_matters: The user must act under time, attention and recovery constraints.
findings.user_impact: Metrics can feel decorative and require extra navigation to act.
findings.recommended_change: Define one evidence-based cross-surface next action only where it helps the user, such as a workout completion cue leading to nutrition logging or XP feedback.
findings.why_this_change: It reduces friction while preserving the current capability contract.
findings.expected_benefit: Clearer task completion and higher confidence.
findings.do_not_break: Existing successful route, state persistence and primary actions
findings.implementation_guidance: Add contextual links such as how intake/XP affects the next workout and one weekly review narrative.

findings.title: Public entry model splits login root from marketing landing
findings.evidence: E61-E62/B08-B14 plus app/page.tsx and site.webmanifest: / renders login for anonymous and authenticated sessions; /landing is reachable with working signup/login CTAs; start_url remains /auth/login.
findings.current_behavior: Two valid public surfaces have different entry jobs, but canonical root and PWA start_url choose login while the marketing proposition lives at /landing.
findings.root_ux_cause: Acquisition and returning-user entry are not explicitly unified or documented at route/manifest level.
findings.why_it_matters: The user must act under time, attention and recovery constraints.
findings.user_impact: Entry intent is ambiguous rather than the landing being absent; users can reach signup/login once they know the route.
findings.recommended_change: Choose and document the canonical model and align root, authenticated redirect, CTA semantics and PWA start_url.
findings.why_this_change: It reduces friction while preserving the current capability contract.
findings.expected_benefit: Clearer acquisition/return intent without removing existing capabilities.
findings.do_not_break: Existing successful route, state persistence and primary actions
findings.implementation_guidance: Add route regression tests for anonymous root, authenticated root, /landing CTAs and manifest start_url before changing behavior.

findings.title: Login offers more social entry choices than signup

findings.current_behavior: E05/E06 show Google/GitHub on login and credential-only signup.
findings.root_ux_cause: Provider actions are implemented separately across entry screens.
findings.why_it_matters: The user must act under time, attention and recovery constraints.
findings.user_impact: Extra navigation and uncertainty about provider account creation.
findings.recommended_change: Align provider actions or explain the single account-creation path.
findings.why_this_change: It reduces friction while preserving the current capability contract.
findings.expected_benefit: Clearer task completion and higher confidence.
findings.do_not_break: Existing successful route, state persistence and primary actions
findings.implementation_guidance: Align provider actions or explain the single account-creation path.

Progress.PRIMARY_USER_GOAL: Understand meaningful change and choose the next training action.
Progress.KPI_INTERPRETABILITY: Good state scan; zeros and missing values need period/baseline context.
Progress.LOW_DATA_STATE: Honest, with missing trend and recommendation cues; no fabricated progress.
Progress.TREND_CLARITY: Charts are discoverable, but interpretation is weaker than metric inventory.
Progress.NEXT_ACTION: Return to workout or act on recommendation; currently implied rather than orchestrated.
Progress.MOBILE_DESKTOP: Readable stacked mobile cards; denser but scannable desktop KPI/chart area.
Progress.LIGHT_DARK_ES_EN: Both themes and ES/EN represented; document lang remains Spanish.
Progress.WHAT_WORKS_WELL: Honest low-data state, visible recommendation, separate chart/measurement/record views.
Progress.FRICTION: The user can see state but not always what changed or what to do next.
Progress.DO_NOT_BREAK: Preserve honest missing-data treatment and avoid decorative or invented progress.
Progress.ANSWER: Partially answers what changed and what to do next.

Nutrition.PRIMARY_USER_GOAL: Understand today's nutrition state and choose log, plan or generation action.
Nutrition.CALORIE_MACRO_CLARITY: Daily state and macro concepts are visible; action meaning could be clearer.
Nutrition.PLAN_LOGGING: Plan access/generation and logging are discoverable; post-write feedback not tested.
Nutrition.RECOMMENDATION_RATIONALE: Recommendations are visible, but selection rationale is not established.
Nutrition.EMPTY_LOW_DATA: Current low-data state is readable; fully empty first-day state not induced.
Nutrition.WORKOUT_RELATIONSHIP: Conceptually adjacent, not presented as coordinated next action.
Nutrition.NEXT_ACTION: User chooses among parallel log/generate/review controls.
Nutrition.MOBILE_DESKTOP: Readable vertical mobile stack; clearer desktop workspace than workout ledger.
Nutrition.LIGHT_DARK_ES_EN: Both themes and representative private locales covered.
Nutrition.WHAT_WORKS_WELL: Daily state, macro/recommendation framing and visible plan/log affordances.
Nutrition.FRICTION: No single highest-value nutrition action dominates.
Nutrition.DO_NOT_BREAK: Keep visible daily state and user-controlled non-clinical actions.
Nutrition.ANSWER: Helps choose a nutrition action, but currently behaves as a parallel dashboard.

Gamification.LEVEL_XP_STREAK: Level, XP and streak are visible status signals.
Gamification.ACHIEVEMENTS: Achievement and history provide a real review destination.
Gamification.PROGRESS_MEANING: Status is clearer than meaning; next unlock/behavior is less explicit.
Gamification.REWARD_FEEDBACK: Display is observed; feedback after earning was not tested.
Gamification.MOTIVATION_PRESSURE: Reinforcement potential is plausible; behavior change and pressure need longitudinal evidence.
Gamification.NEXT_ACTION: Review achievements or return to training; bridge is implicit.
Gamification.WORKOUT_PROGRESS_RELATION: Separate from workout completion and Progress workspace in the observed UI.
Gamification.MOBILE_DESKTOP_LIGHT_DARK_ES_EN: Readable stacked mobile and compact desktop views in both theme/locale families.
Gamification.FRICTION: Surface shows progress without making the next rewarding behavior unmistakable.
Gamification.DO_NOT_BREAK: Keep rewards subordinate to meaningful training behavior.
Gamification.ANSWER: More than decoration, but not yet proven behavior guidance.
